title: "Hephaestus plot documents"

A [hephaestus](https://github.com/posit-dev/hephaestus) plot document
(`.hep`) stores a plot's data, scales and theme rather than a picture
of it. Quarto lays the plot out itself at render time and writes an SVG
next to this page.

## A figure, with a caption and a cross-reference

@fig-readings is referenced like any other figure.

![Simulated sensor readings, one panel of points and one of trend lines.](figs/readings.hep){#fig-readings}

## The same document at an explicit size

`width` and `height` (pixels) set the size the plot is laid out at. The
plot re-flows to fit — compare the tick density with @fig-readings —
rather than being scaled down:

![](figs/readings.hep){width=420 height=260}

## Left alone

An ordinary image is untouched, and a `.hep` that does not exist warns
(`Q-18-1`) and is left as written, so the rest of the page still renders:

![](figs/does-not-exist.hep)
